question: Swedish nouns take either en or ett. What became of the masculine and feminine genders Old Swedish had?
answer: They merged into one, the common gender. Old Swedish had three genders, like German; as endings wore down, masculine and feminine forms fell together, leaving en words and ett words, the old neuter. Danish and standard Dutch went much the same way. A Swede now says en man and en kvinna with a single article.
move: When two categories stop sounding different, they soon stop being different.
source: Holmes & Hinchliffe, Swedish: A Comprehensive Grammar
reference: Holmes & Hinchliffe, Swedish: A Comprehensive Grammar, 3rd edition, Routledge, 2013
